meta.name: Hero MotoCorp Ltd
meta.about: Hero Moto Corp earlier also known as “Hero Honda” is one of India’s first motorcycle manufacturers. The company started in 1984 as a Technological collaboration with Honda, Japan. Before this collaboration, Hero was selling Cycles under the brand name, Hero Cycles. In 2011, Honda group sold its 26% stake in the company to the Munjals (promoters) and ended the JV. Post the termination of JV, the name of the company was changed to Hero Motocorp. [1] [2]

profile.summary: World's largest maker of motorcycles and scooters by volume for 25 years (64.69 lakh units in FY26). Brands: Splendor, HF Deluxe, Passion (100-110cc), Glamour, Super Splendor, Xtreme 125R (125cc), Xtreme 160R/250R, Xpulse, Karizma, Mavrick and the Harley-Davidson X440 (premium), Destini, Xoom, Pleasure+ (scooters), VIDA (electric scooters). assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Hero MotoCorp (consolidated, INR crore; Screener basis). Base year FY26A. Forecast profit EXCLUDES the share of associates (Hero FinCorp, Ather Energy, Euler Motors): those stakes are valued separately at market/book in the target (street method). Volume x realisation build by segment in volumeBuild; HEROMOTOCO.ctx.js checks that it reproduces model revenue.

volume._why: Sum of the segment build (volumeBuild). FY27: Apr-Aug 2026 dispatches 27.79 lakh (+17%) but H2 laps the post-GST surge (Q3FY26 +16%, Q4FY26 +24%), Aug-26 was only +2.7% and the 2026 monsoon ended ~13% short; Sep-Mar assumed +3.5%. FY28-29: industry ~5%, Hero helped by scooters, VIDA and premium, dragged by entry bikes.

assumptions._revPerUnitWhy: Revenue (incl. parts and services) per vehicle, from the build: FY27 ~5% ICE price increases already taken (4.5% blended since Feb-26), early double-digit EV price rises, mix shift to scooters/EV/125cc/premium and parts +20%; FY28-29 ~3% price plus mix.

volumeBuild._note: FY26 units by segment: SIAM data compiled by Emkay Research (9-Aug-2026; total 64.66 lakh vs the company's 64.69 lakh). Realisations are net revenue per unit (ex-GST, after dealer margin). EV (Q1FY27 EV revenue Rs660 cr on 56,837 units = Rs1.16 lakh; FY26 assumed ~10% lower after early double-digit price rises) and exports (FY26 ~Rs3,500 cr on 4.02 lakh units, CFO, May-2026 call) are disclosed or derived; domestic ICE segment realisations are not disclosed: the FY26 domestic ICE revenue pool (two-wheeler sales Rs39,085 cr less exports and EV) is spread by a price index built from Hero's model-wise GST price cuts of Sep-2025 (HF Deluxe Rs5,805, Splendor+ Rs6,820, Glamour X Rs7,813, Xtreme 125R Rs8,010, Destini 125 Rs7,197, Xoom 110 Rs6,597, Xtreme 160R Rs10,985: cuts are ~7.8% of ex-showroom price, so they scale with price).

parts._why: Spare parts revenue FY26 Rs6,592 cr (consolidated; +6%); Q1FY27 parts, accessories and merchandise +30%, July ~25%; GPC 2.0 (Rs750 cr) doubles capacity by end-2027.

other._why: Services (extended warranty, AMC, dealer support: Rs1,371 cr) and other operating revenue incl. export incentives (Rs363 cr) in FY26.

assumptions._marginWhy: Consolidated. FY26 14.9% (standalone 14.7%: ICE 17.0% less ~2.3 pts of VIDA losses). Q1FY27 13.3% after a 300 bp gross-margin hit from West Asia-linked commodity inflation (ICE 15.9%). FY27: Q2 cost pressure offset by mix and cost cuts, H2 price increases; VIDA losses ~Rs900 cr. FY28-29: commodity relief, VIDA scale and PLI (13% of EV revenue) take the margin back into the 14-16% medium-term band, at its lower half.
assumptions._capexWhy: FY27 guidance Rs1,500 cr (EV, scooter and Splendor capacity, GPC 2.0 parts centre Rs750 cr, Neemrana premium line); FY26 actual Rs1,100 cr; ~2% of revenue thereafter.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Yield on earning treasury (debt funds, bonds, deposits). FY26 treasury income ~Rs1,144 cr (interest Rs293 cr, dividends Rs23 cr, gains on sale Rs128 cr, fair-value gains Rs533 cr before the Rs222 cr Zero Motorcycles write-down, less ~Rs54 cr gain on BSE shares) on ~Rs13,700 cr average earning treasury = 8.4%. FY27 8.5% (Q1FY27 other income Rs460 cr ran above that); 8% from FY28 as FY26-27 mark-to-market gains came with falling yields.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Model treasury (cash + investments - borrowings) includes strategic stakes that earn no interest: associates at book (Rs3,901 cr at Mar-26), Euler CCPS Rs210 cr, BSE Rs170 cr, Zero Rs19 cr, Gogoro Rs2 cr = Rs4,302 cr; plus Ather shares bought in Aug-26 (Rs1,758 cr block from GIC + Rs240 cr warrant money) and the Rs720 cr warrant balance assumed paid mid-FY28. Line = -(that year's yield) x average non-earning stakes (FY27 Rs5,468 cr, FY28 Rs6,660 cr, FY29 Rs7,020 cr). Share of associates' profit/loss is excluded from our EPS (stakes valued separately).

stakes._note: Value added to the core P/E (street method). Used by tools/authoring/HEROMOTOCO.stakes.js to set the composite P/E multiple in valuation.blend (engine has no add-on line).
stakes._coreWhy: Base 15.0x: own one-year-forward P/E median since Apr-2021 on EPS before associates and one-offs (16.4x; the house forwardMedian on reported EPS is 16.7x, and 17.0x adjusting only one-offs; no trough years) x (1 - 6.9%), the median de-rating of the seven other auto OEMs at 30-Sep-2026 = 15.2x, rounded to the nearest half-turn. The core basis is used because our EPS excludes associates and the stakes are added at market. Bull 18.0x and bear 12.5x = the 75th and 25th percentiles of the same core history (19.2x, 13.7x) after the same de-rating.

ather._why: NSE close 30-Sep-2026 Rs1,425. Shares: 11,50,83,252 at Mar-26 (AR FY26 note 9A; 29.48% at Jun-26) + 1,18,80,000 bought from GIC at Rs1,480 on 28-Aug-2026 (Rs1,758 cr). Warrants: 76,19,047 at Rs1,260 allotted 25-Aug-2026, 25% paid, Rs945 a share payable on conversion within 18 months (valued at intrinsic value). 20% holding discount = house precedent (Tata Chemicals' Rallis and quoted shares) and Motilal Oswal/Emkay; Choice uses 30%.

hfcl._why: Unlisted. Net assets Rs5,900 cr at Mar-26 (AR FY26 note 9A); Hero owns 40.45% (5,24,31,893 shares). FY26 loss Rs226 cr; IPO approved by SEBI in 2025 but not launched by Sep-26. Valued at 1.0x book less 20% (street range Rs55-215 a share: PL Rs55, Choice Rs59, MOSL Rs89, Emkay Rs215).

others._why: Carrying values at Mar-26 (AR FY26 notes 9A/9B): Euler Motors associate Rs401 cr + Series E CCPS Rs210 cr, BSE shares Rs170 cr, Zero Motorcycles Rs19 cr, Gogoro Rs2 cr.

assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs78 cr (leases and subsidiaries' working-capital loans); Q1FY27 Rs21 cr.
assumptions._taxWhy: Standalone effective rate 24.4% in FY26 and 25.6% in Q1FY27 (new regime, 25.17%).
assumptions._payoutWhy: Policy of 70%+ payout of standalone profit (CFO, May-2026); FY26 DPS Rs185 (interim Rs110 + final Rs75) = 70% of standalone EPS of Rs263.

dcf._why: Cost of equity 6.5% + 0.85 x 6% = 11.6%; net cash, so WACC = Ke. Nominal revenue growth fades to 7% by FY42 (Hero grew revenue 5.2% a year in FY16-26 and 8.9% in FY21-26: ~3% volume + ~4% price/mix) and the EBITDA margin to 14%, the bottom of the 14-16% band, as the EV shift squeezes the ICE franchise; terminal growth 5%.
dcf._betaWhy: Hero's two-year weekly beta has been below 1 (defensive commuter demand, net cash); 0.85 as for Maruti.
dcf._tgWhy: Two-wheeler penetration is still rising, but Hero's core (commuter motorcycles) is losing share of the market to scooters, EVs and premium bikes.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Rural demand shrugs off the weak monsoon, scooters, VIDA (PLI on the whole range from Dec-26) and premium launches keep gaining share, exports recover; EBITDA margin back to ~15% by FY28. Ather valued at a 10% holding discount.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: The weak 2026 monsoon and the end of the GST boost stall entry and deluxe motorcycles, TVS/Bajaj/Ather out-launch VIDA, commodity costs stay high; margins stuck near 13%. Ather valued at a 30% holding discount and Hero FinCorp at 0.7x book.

methods.name: P/E (15x core) + stakes
methods.why: How the street values Hero: P/E on FY28E/Jun-28E core EPS (16-18x: PL 16x, Motilal Oswal, Emkay and Choice 18x) plus the Ather and Hero FinCorp stakes at a 20-30% holding discount. Ours: 15.0x Sep-28E EPS before associates (own forward median since 2021 on that basis 16.4x x 0.931 sector de-rating) plus stakes of ~Rs870 a share (Ather at the 30-Sep close of Rs1,425 less 20%, Hero FinCorp at 1.0x Mar-26 book less 20%, Euler and other holdings at book). ENGINE WORKAROUND: the engine has no add-on line, so the multiple shown is a composite = 15.0x + stakes per share / Sep-28E EPS of each scenario (set by tools/authoring/HEROMOTOCO.stakes.js). Bull core 18x, bear 12.5x.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: 9.0x Sep-28E EBITDA plus model net cash (which carries the stakes at book, not market). Derivation: Hero's 12.9x median trailing EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021 x 0.931 sector de-rating = 12.0x trailing, restated for Sep-28E EBITDA being ~30% above the twelve months to Jun-26 (Rs7,090 cr) = 9.2x, rounded. Bull 10x / bear 8.5x from the 75th/25th percentiles (14.3x, 11.9x) on the same basis.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests cash-flow support: 15-year FCFF, cost of equity 11.6%, terminal growth 5.5%. Net cash includes the stakes at book value.

cover.headline: You pay for the core and get the stakes free: a cheap, cash-rich leader whose home market is shrinking
cover.lead: Hero MotoCorp is the world's largest two-wheeler maker (64.69 lakh units in FY26) and owns India's 100-110cc motorcycle market (~96% of it). That segment is losing ground: commuter motorcycles fell from 42% to 32% of industry volume in five years and Hero's overall share from 31% to 23%. The GST cut of Sep-2025 and fast gains in scooters, 125cc and VIDA electric scooters lifted Q1FY27 volume 23% and revenue 36%, but August dispatches rose only 2.7%, commodity costs cut the margin to 13.3% and the 2026 monsoon ended ~13% short. Hero also owns ~32% of Ather Energy (worth ~₹18,458 cr at the 30-Sep close) and 40% of Hero FinCorp. The street values it on **P/E on FY28E core EPS (16-18x) plus the stakes**. We do the same: **15x Sep-28E EPS of ₹349.4 (₹5,241) plus ₹868 a share for the stakes** gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}})**: **we initiate with BUY.** Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹5,359, DCF ₹7,399. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: The core is priced like a business in decline
arguments.p: Take out the stakes (₹868 a share after a 20% discount) and ₹5,241 buys the core at 13.3x our FY28E EPS, against a 16.4x median forward multiple since 2021 on the same basis. Our 15x already includes the 7% de-rating of auto stocks.

Record share in 100-110cc (96%), 125cc back to 18%, ICE scooters doubled to 7%, VIDA ~11% of e-scooters, parts +30% in Q1FY27, exports up 39% in FY26. 35% ROCE, negative working capital and a 70% payout (~4% yield at our FY28E DPS).

arguments.h: But growth is modest and fragile
arguments.p: We forecast volume +{{as.volume.growth.0|n1}}% in FY27E and ~5% a year after; EPS ~9% a year to FY29E. H2FY27 laps the post-GST surge, the monsoon was the weakest since 2015 and TVS out-sold Hero in August. The EV shift erodes the 100cc moat over time.

arguments.h: Ather is a big, volatile part of the value
arguments.p: Ather is ~₹734 a share of our target (12%) after a 20% discount; at ~15x trailing sales it can move 30% either way. Every ₹100 on Ather's price is ~₹50 on our target. Hero FinCorp (₹95) made a loss in FY26.

catalysts: Festive season (Navratri to Diwali falls in Oct-Nov 2026, later than 2025) and Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): whether retail holds up after a weak monsoon, and the margin after Q2's "marginal uptick" in input costs.
Monthly dispatches: August was +2.7% with exports -24.5%; motorcycles need to grow again against the post-GST base from October.
VIDA: capacity from ~30k to ~45k a month by Q4FY27, PLI on 100% of the range by Dec-2026, EBITDA-breakeven ambition by year-end.
Premium launches over the next 12 months (new premium business head from Aug-2026); Harley-Davidson range.
Ather: share price, conversion of the 76.19 lakh warrants (₹720 cr due within 18 months) and its own results; Hero FinCorp IPO, which SEBI approved in 2025 but which had not launched by Sep-2026.

sections.title: What Hero does: 65 lakh two-wheelers a year, three-quarters of them 100cc-class commuter bikes

blocks.p: Hero designs, makes and sells motorcycles and scooters, and the spare parts for the ~130 million Hero vehicles sold since 1984. FY26 consolidated revenue was ₹47,411 cr: ₹39,085 cr from vehicles (82%), ₹6,592 cr from spare parts (14%) and ₹1,734 cr from services and export incentives. It has six plants in India plus Colombia and Bangladesh, ~8.63 mn units of capacity and 14,000+ customer touchpoints, with a point of sale in 93% of India's talukas. The parent company (standalone) is ~99% of the group; subsidiaries in Colombia, Bangladesh, the US and a German R&D centre added ~₹580 cr of revenue in FY26.

Volume is concentrated in one product family. sections.title: Commuter motorcycles: a near-monopoly in a segment that is losing share of the market

blocks.p: Hero sold 54.2 lakh entry, deluxe and 125cc motorcycles in India in FY26, ~84% of its volume and, we estimate, ~65% of revenue. In 100-110cc (Splendor, Passion) its share rose from 87% in FY21 to 96.4% in Q1FY27: nine of ten buyers choose Hero for mileage, reliability and resale value. In Q1FY27 deluxe volume grew 20.5%, Splendor 15% and 125cc 45% (share back to 17.7% from 12.8% a year earlier on Glamour X and Xtreme 125R), while entry HF Deluxe fell 19% as buyers traded up after the GST cut. Hero added 2,000 units a day of Splendor capacity in Q1FY27 and launched E20-E85 flex-fuel Splendor and HF Deluxe versions in July.

blocks.p: The problem is the segment, not Hero's position in it. Commuter motorcycles were 42% of industry volume in FY21 and 32% in Q1FY27, as rising incomes push buyers to scooters, 125cc and premium bikes and as women and urban buyers choose scooters. Entry (economy) bikes have shrunk to 5% of the market. Price increases since February 2026 (~4.5%) and higher fuel prices test affordability; Hero cut the price of one HF Deluxe variant in some states in July to pull first-time buyers back. Electrification is not an immediate threat here (no affordable electric commuter bike yet, long rural rides, heavy loads), but Hero itself plans electric motorcycles from FY28.

sections.title: Scooters and VIDA: growing fast from far behind; VIDA still loses ~₹230 cr a quarter

blocks.p: Scooters are 31.5% of the market and Hero's share was only 4.6% (ICE) in Q1FY26. Since then Destini 125 and the Xoom range lifted ICE scooter dispatches 84% in Q1FY27 (share 6.9%); Destini capacity has been doubled and Xoom raised 50%, with channel stock at half the normal level. In electric scooters VIDA's VAHAN registrations rose from 18,783 (FY24) to 50,800 (FY25) and 1,49,341 (FY26); Q1FY27 dispatches were 56,837 (+151%) and retail is now >20,000 a month (~11% share, #4 behind TVS, Bajaj and Ather). The low-cost VX2 with battery-as-a-service (from ₹0.9 a km) and removable batteries drove the jump; Hero was also less hit than rivals by the 2025 rare-earth magnet shortage.

blocks.p: VIDA is still a cost centre. Management puts the "P&L investment" at ~₹220 cr in Q4FY26 and ~₹230 cr in Q1FY27, a 2.4-2.6 point drag on group margin; the EBITDA loss per unit fell from ~₹50,000 to ~₹40,000. EV revenue was ~₹660 cr in Q1FY27 (5% of revenue). Three levers: PLI (₹48 cr accrued in Q1FY27 on 60% of the range; ~13% of EV revenue once the whole range qualifies by Dec-2026), scale (capacity ~30k a month from August, ~45k by Q4FY27) and cost reduction; some models are already gross-margin positive and management aims for breakeven "by the end of the year". sections.title: Premium, exports and parts: parts is the hidden gem; premium remains a gap

blocks.p: **Premium (>125cc)** is the most profitable part of the market (13.5% of industry volume) and Hero's weakest: 71,320 units in FY26 and a 1.5% share in Q1FY27, down from 3.8% in FY21. The Harley-Davidson X440 range (made by Hero) grew 26% in FY26, helped by the new X440T variant; the Xtreme 250R and Mavrick 440 did not move share. A new premium head (ex-Royal Enfield) took over in Aug-2026 with "many" launches promised over 12 months. **Exports** (4.0 lakh units, ~₹3,500 cr in FY26) grew ~40% a year in FY25-26 and 63% in Q1FY27, then fell 14% in July and 24.5% in August 2026. Hero entered Germany and Ecuador in 2026; Colombia, Bangladesh and Nepal are the core markets.

**Parts, accessories and merchandise (PAM)** earned ₹6,592 cr in FY26 (AR, consolidated; ~₹6,200 cr per management), 14% of revenue, and grew 30% in Q1FY27 (₹1,689 cr) and ~25% in July. Management estimates that about half of Hero-parts demand is still met by the grey market; the ₹750 cr second parts centre at Tirupati (foundation stone 1-Jul-2026, commissioning by end-2027) more than doubles capacity. Parts carry well above-average margins, which is why ICE margins held at 15.9% despite the commodity hit.

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Hero has a real moat, but a narrow one. In 100-110cc motorcycles its brand, rural reach, service network, resale values and scale give it ~96% of the segment and the lowest cost per unit in the industry; nobody has dented that in 15 years. Outside that segment it has no structural advantage: in scooters, premium bikes, exports and EVs it is a late, small challenger that wins share only when it out-spends and out-launches rivals. Because its core segment is shrinking as a share of the market, the moat protects cash flow, not growth.

sections.title: A decade of slow growth, then FY26: record volumes after the GST cut

blocks.p: Hero's consolidated revenue grew from ₹28,457 cr in FY16 to ₹47,411 cr in FY26, only 5.2% a year, and profit from ₹3,112 cr to ₹5,776 cr (6.4% a year). For most of the decade volumes went nowhere: a new emission standard (BS6, Apr-2020), Covid and a rural slowdown pushed revenue down to ₹29,551 cr in FY22. The recovery since then has come in three steps: price increases and a better mix (FY23-24, EBITDA margin from 11% to 14%), a steady FY25 (+8%) and the September-2025 GST cut, which lifted FY26 volumes 9.6% to 64.69 lakh and revenue 16%. Note that reported FY26 profit includes a one-time ₹722 cr gain from the dilution of Hero's stake in its associates (Ather's IPO and a private placement): before associates and one-offs, FY26 EPS was ~₹283, not ₹287.

blocks.p: Hero needs little capital: capex was ₹2,745 cr over FY24-26 against ₹17,535 cr of operating cash flow. Dividends took ₹9,009 cr over FY24-26; investments in group companies and start-ups (Ather, Euler Motors, Zero Motorcycles) ₹1,483 cr. In FY27 the pattern changes: ₹1,998 cr went into Ather in August-2026 alone (₹1,758 cr of shares from GIC plus 25% of ₹960 cr of warrants), with ₹720 cr more due if the warrants are converted, and capex rises to the guided ₹1,500 cr.

Management has chosen to own a third of Ather (₹2,700 cr committed in 2026 at ₹1,260-1,480 a share) while also building VIDA, and to fund Hero FinCorp (which lost ₹226 cr in FY26). sections.title: Earnings quality: clean and cash-backed, but reported profit mixes in associates and one-offs

bullets: **Cash backs profit.** Operating cash flow was 144% of reported profit in FY26 (₹2,375 cr working-capital inflow as payables rose), 98% in FY25 and 132% in FY24; over FY15-26 cash from operations (₹46,845 cr) exceeded profit (₹41,828 cr).

**Associates sit inside consolidated profit.** Hero equity-accounts Hero FinCorp, Ather and Euler: their share of profit/loss was −₹120 cr (FY24), −₹161 cr (FY25) and +₹385 cr (FY26, including a ₹722 cr gain when Ather's IPO and a private placement diluted Hero's stake). Excluding them and the one-offs, FY26 EPS was ~₹283, not the reported ₹287. Our forecasts exclude associates and value the stakes separately.

**Other income is sizeable and volatile.** ₹1,058 cr in FY26 (consolidated, 14% of pre-tax profit): ₹293 cr interest, ₹128 cr gains on sale and ₹533 cr fair-value gains on debt funds, net of a ₹222 cr write-down of the Zero Motorcycles stake after a dilutive round. Mark-to-market gains rise and fall with bond yields.
**One-offs:** ₹119 cr labour-code charge (FY26), ₹160 cr VRS (FY24). Small.

**Minorities and share count.** Screener's FY26 "Net Profit" (₹5,776 cr) is before ₹34 cr of minorities; EPS uses ₹5,742 cr. The engine's implied share count (20.13 cr) is 0.6% above the actual 20.01 cr; below our 1% threshold, so no adjustment.

**Tax:** an income-tax demand from a 2022 search (₹178 cr in FY25, ₹27 cr outstanding) is under appeal with no provision; PLI incentives are booked as income (₹48 cr in Q1FY27, growing as the whole VIDA range qualifies).

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: GREEN.** Unqualified audit, strong cash conversion, negative working capital and a simple balance sheet. Two things to adjust for: associates (including one-off dilution gains) in consolidated profit, and mark-to-market treasury income. We strip out the first and normalise the second.

sections.title: The stakes: ~₹868 a share after a 20% discount, over 80% of it in Ather

blocks.p: Hero owns three large minority stakes, all **equity-accounted**: the consolidated accounts carry them at cost plus Hero's share of their profits or losses (₹3,901 cr at Mar-2026: Hero FinCorp ₹2,407 cr, Ather ₹1,093 cr, Euler ₹401 cr), and one line in the P&L, "share of profit/loss of associates", carries Hero's share of their results: +₹385 cr in FY26 (Hero FinCorp +₹70 cr, Ather +₹461 cr including the ₹722 cr dilution gain, Euler −₹109 cr) and −₹44 cr in Q1FY27. Book value says nothing about what the stakes are worth, and the P&L line is mostly noise (Ather's losses, one-off gains). So, like the street, we take them out of EPS and value them separately at the 30-Sep-2026 market price or on book.

At ₹1,425 Ather is worth ~₹56,447 cr, ~15x its FY26 revenue of ₹3,672 cr (net loss ₹517 cr): a growth valuation that can swing hard. We apply a 20% holding discount (no control, tax on any sale, Hero is a long-term holder), as the street (Motilal Oswal, Emkay) and our own Tata Chemicals report do.

**Hero FinCorp** lends to two-wheeler buyers, MSMEs and individuals (FY26 total income ₹9,583 cr). It lost ₹226 cr in FY26 on high credit costs, paid Hero only ₹6 cr of dividends, and its IPO (approved by SEBI in 2025, ~₹3,668 cr) had not launched by Sep-2026. We value Hero's 40.45% at 1.0x Mar-26 book less 20% (₹95 a share), inside the street's ₹55-215 range; book is generous for a loss-making lender and our bear case uses 0.7x.

sections.title: Valuation: 15x core earnings plus ₹868 of stakes gives {{dcf.tp|inr}}

blocks.h: Method: the street's, on our numbers

blocks.p: We value Hero the way the street does: **P/E on core earnings plus the stakes**. Core earnings = our consolidated EPS before the share of associates, for the twelve months the market will look at in September 2027 (Sep-28E: half FY28E, half FY29E) = ₹349.4. The stakes are valued separately (previous chapter). Because the engine has no "plus stakes" line, the P/E line in our model and Excel carries a **composite multiple** of 17.5x = 15x + ₹868 ÷ ₹349.4 (bull 20.5x, bear 15.0x); it is arithmetic, not a view that Hero deserves 17.5x.

growth.text: Revenue compounded at 5.2% a year over 10 years (5y: 8.9%, 3y: 11.5%), from ₹28,457 cr to ₹47,411 cr.
Profit grew 6.4% a year over the same decade — faster than revenue, i.e. operating leverage.
Worst profit year: FY22 (-20.7%); best: FY24 (+33.6%).

margins.text: EBITDA margin has ranged 11.0%–16.4% since FY15 (peak FY18, trough FY22); FY26 was 14.9%.
Q1FY27 operating margin of 13.0% is lower than 75.6% of the 86 quarters on record — near the bottom of its history.
Raw-material cost moved from 66% to 67% of sales in FY26 (+1 pts) — the single biggest swing factor in the cost base.
Other income (largely treasury yield on the cash pile) made up 17.6% of pre-tax profit in FY26; reported profit flatters core operations.

returns.text: ROE was 28.3% in FY26 (range 14.9–40.5% since FY15).
Stripping out cash and investments, return on operating capital was 265.5% vs headline ROCE of 35.0% — the idle cash is diluting reported returns.
DuPont FY26: net margin 12.2% × asset turnover 1.5x × leverage 1.5x.

balance.text: Net cash of ₹19,274 cr (cash + investments less borrowings), 89.2% of net worth.

cash.text: Over 12 years the business generated ₹46,845 cr of operating cash flow (112.0% of reported profit), spent ₹11,701 cr on capex and paid ₹25,448 cr in dividends.
FY26 capex was 1.3x depreciation and 2.3% of sales — maintenance-level spending.
Cash conversion cycle of -40 days in FY26 — suppliers fund the working capital.

valuation.text: P/E of 19.4x vs 10-year median 20.2x (range 9.4–30.0x); cheaper than 60.2% of that period.
EV/EBITDA of 12.9x vs 10-year median 13.0x (range 5.8–19.1x); cheaper than 50.2% of that period.
P/B of 5.0x vs 10-year median 4.5x (range 2.2–8.7x); cheaper than 34.9% of that period.
At its 10-year median P/E on current earnings, the stock would be ~₹5,457 vs ₹5,241 today (4.1%).

price.text: Stock down 5.6% over 1 year; 5y CAGR 13.0%, 10y CAGR 4.4%. Currently 17.5% below its all-time high of ₹6,351.
Versus BSE-500: -5.6% vs -2.2% over 1 year; since 2019, 7.5% vs 12.4% a year.

ownership.text: Foreign institutions raised their stake from 28.3% to 31.1% over 11 quarters.
Domestic institutions cut their stake from 28.1% to 24.3% over 11 quarters.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Hero MotoCorp (consolidated, INR crore; Screener basis). Base year FY26A. Forecast profit EXCLUDES the share of associates (Hero FinCorp, Ather Energy, Euler Motors): those stakes are valued separately at market/book in the target (street method). Volume x realisation build by segment in volumeBuild; HEROMOTOCO.ctx.js checks that it reproduces model revenue.

volume._why: Sum of the segment build (volumeBuild). FY27: Apr-Aug 2026 dispatches 27.79 lakh (+17%) but H2 laps the post-GST surge (Q3FY26 +16%, Q4FY26 +24%), Aug-26 was only +2.7% and the 2026 monsoon ended ~13% short; Sep-Mar assumed +3.5%. FY28-29: industry ~5%, Hero helped by scooters, VIDA and premium, dragged by entry bikes.

assumptions._revPerUnitWhy: Revenue (incl. parts and services) per vehicle, from the build: FY27 ~5% ICE price increases already taken (4.5% blended since Feb-26), early double-digit EV price rises, mix shift to scooters/EV/125cc/premium and parts +20%; FY28-29 ~3% price plus mix.

volumeBuild._note: FY26 units by segment: SIAM data compiled by Emkay Research (9-Aug-2026; total 64.66 lakh vs the company's 64.69 lakh). Realisations are net revenue per unit (ex-GST, after dealer margin). EV (Q1FY27 EV revenue Rs660 cr on 56,837 units = Rs1.16 lakh; FY26 assumed ~10% lower after early double-digit price rises) and exports (FY26 ~Rs3,500 cr on 4.02 lakh units, CFO, May-2026 call) are disclosed or derived; domestic ICE segment realisations are not disclosed: the FY26 domestic ICE revenue pool (two-wheeler sales Rs39,085 cr less exports and EV) is spread by a price index built from Hero's model-wise GST price cuts of Sep-2025 (HF Deluxe Rs5,805, Splendor+ Rs6,820, Glamour X Rs7,813, Xtreme 125R Rs8,010, Destini 125 Rs7,197, Xoom 110 Rs6,597, Xtreme 160R Rs10,985: cuts are ~7.8% of ex-showroom price, so they scale with price).

segments.name: Domestic motorcycles: entry 100cc (HF Deluxe)
segments._why: Q1FY27 -19%: buyers trade up to Splendor; a tactical HF Deluxe price cut in Jul-26 helped, but a weak monsoon hurts the poorest buyers first.

segments.name: Domestic motorcycles: deluxe 100-110cc (Splendor, Passion)
segments._why: Q1FY27 +20.5% (Splendor +15%, 96% segment share); +2,000/day Splendor capacity; H2 laps the GST surge; long run ~3-4%.

segments.name: Domestic motorcycles: 125cc (Glamour, Super Splendor, Xtreme 125R)
segments._why: Q1FY27 +45%: share recovered from 12.8% (Q1FY26) to 17.7%; more refreshes planned for Q2FY27.

segments.name: Domestic motorcycles: premium >125cc (Xtreme 160/250, Xpulse, Karizma, Harley X440, Mavrick)
segments._why: Q1FY27 +27% but share only 1.5%; new premium head (Aug-26) and launches over the next 12 months. Index ~2x Splendor (Xtreme 160R ~1.6x, Xtreme 250R ~2.1x, X440 higher).

segments.name: Domestic ICE scooters (Destini 125, Xoom, Pleasure+)
segments._why: Q1FY27 +84% (share 6.9%); Destini capacity doubled and Xoom +50%; channel stock half of normal.

segments.name: VIDA electric scooters
segments._why: Apr-Aug 2026 ~1.05 lakh; capacity 30k/month from Aug-26, 45k/month by Q4FY27; ~11% VAHAN share. FY27E ~2.8 lakh.

segments.name: Exports (global business)
segments._why: Q1FY27 +63% but Jul-26 -14% and Aug-26 -24.5%; Apr-Aug +20%. Management aims for ~40% a year; we assume a slowdown.

parts._why: Spare parts revenue FY26 Rs6,592 cr (consolidated; +6%); Q1FY27 parts, accessories and merchandise +30%, July ~25%; GPC 2.0 (Rs750 cr) doubles capacity by end-2027.

other._why: Services (extended warranty, AMC, dealer support: Rs1,371 cr) and other operating revenue incl. export incentives (Rs363 cr) in FY26.

assumptions._marginWhy: Consolidated. FY26 14.9% (standalone 14.7%: ICE 17.0% less ~2.3 pts of VIDA losses). Q1FY27 13.3% after a 300 bp gross-margin hit from West Asia-linked commodity inflation (ICE 15.9%). FY27: Q2 cost pressure offset by mix and cost cuts, H2 price increases; VIDA losses ~Rs900 cr. FY28-29: commodity relief, VIDA scale and PLI (13% of EV revenue) take the margin back into the 14-16% medium-term band, at its lower half.
assumptions._capexWhy: FY27 guidance Rs1,500 cr (EV, scooter and Splendor capacity, GPC 2.0 parts centre Rs750 cr, Neemrana premium line); FY26 actual Rs1,100 cr; ~2% of revenue thereafter.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Yield on earning treasury (debt funds, bonds, deposits). FY26 treasury income ~Rs1,144 cr (interest Rs293 cr, dividends Rs23 cr, gains on sale Rs128 cr, fair-value gains Rs533 cr before the Rs222 cr Zero Motorcycles write-down, less ~Rs54 cr gain on BSE shares) on ~Rs13,700 cr average earning treasury = 8.4%. FY27 8.5% (Q1FY27 other income Rs460 cr ran above that); 8% from FY28 as FY26-27 mark-to-market gains came with falling yields.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Model treasury (cash + investments - borrowings) includes strategic stakes that earn no interest: associates at book (Rs3,901 cr at Mar-26), Euler CCPS Rs210 cr, BSE Rs170 cr, Zero Rs19 cr, Gogoro Rs2 cr = Rs4,302 cr; plus Ather shares bought in Aug-26 (Rs1,758 cr block from GIC + Rs240 cr warrant money) and the Rs720 cr warrant balance assumed paid mid-FY28. Line = -(that year's yield) x average non-earning stakes (FY27 Rs5,468 cr, FY28 Rs6,660 cr, FY29 Rs7,020 cr). Share of associates' profit/loss is excluded from our EPS (stakes valued separately).

stakes._note: Value added to the core P/E (street method). Used by tools/authoring/HEROMOTOCO.stakes.js to set the composite P/E multiple in valuation.blend (engine has no add-on line).
stakes._coreWhy: Base 15.0x: own one-year-forward P/E median since Apr-2021 on EPS before associates and one-offs (16.4x; the house forwardMedian on reported EPS is 16.7x, and 17.0x adjusting only one-offs; no trough years) x (1 - 6.9%), the median de-rating of the seven other auto OEMs at 30-Sep-2026 = 15.2x, rounded to the nearest half-turn. The core basis is used because our EPS excludes associates and the stakes are added at market. Bull 18.0x and bear 12.5x = the 75th and 25th percentiles of the same core history (19.2x, 13.7x) after the same de-rating.

ather._why: NSE close 30-Sep-2026 Rs1,425. Shares: 11,50,83,252 at Mar-26 (AR FY26 note 9A; 29.48% at Jun-26) + 1,18,80,000 bought from GIC at Rs1,480 on 28-Aug-2026 (Rs1,758 cr). Warrants: 76,19,047 at Rs1,260 allotted 25-Aug-2026, 25% paid, Rs945 a share payable on conversion within 18 months (valued at intrinsic value). 20% holding discount = house precedent (Tata Chemicals' Rallis and quoted shares) and Motilal Oswal/Emkay; Choice uses 30%.

hfcl._why: Unlisted. Net assets Rs5,900 cr at Mar-26 (AR FY26 note 9A); Hero owns 40.45% (5,24,31,893 shares). FY26 loss Rs226 cr; IPO approved by SEBI in 2025 but not launched by Sep-26. Valued at 1.0x book less 20% (street range Rs55-215 a share: PL Rs55, Choice Rs59, MOSL Rs89, Emkay Rs215).

others._why: Carrying values at Mar-26 (AR FY26 notes 9A/9B): Euler Motors associate Rs401 cr + Series E CCPS Rs210 cr, BSE shares Rs170 cr, Zero Motorcycles Rs19 cr, Gogoro Rs2 cr.

assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs78 cr (leases and subsidiaries' working-capital loans); Q1FY27 Rs21 cr.
assumptions._taxWhy: Standalone effective rate 24.4% in FY26 and 25.6% in Q1FY27 (new regime, 25.17%).
assumptions._payoutWhy: Policy of 70%+ payout of standalone profit (CFO, May-2026); FY26 DPS Rs185 (interim Rs110 + final Rs75) = 70% of standalone EPS of Rs263.

dcf._why: Cost of equity 6.5% + 0.85 x 6% = 11.6%; net cash, so WACC = Ke. Nominal revenue growth fades to 7% by FY42 (Hero grew revenue 5.2% a year in FY16-26 and 8.9% in FY21-26: ~3% volume + ~4% price/mix) and the EBITDA margin to 14%, the bottom of the 14-16% band, as the EV shift squeezes the ICE franchise; terminal growth 5%.
dcf._betaWhy: Hero's two-year weekly beta has been below 1 (defensive commuter demand, net cash); 0.85 as for Maruti.
dcf._tgWhy: Two-wheeler penetration is still rising, but Hero's core (commuter motorcycles) is losing share of the market to scooters, EVs and premium bikes.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Rural demand shrugs off the weak monsoon, scooters, VIDA (PLI on the whole range from Dec-26) and premium launches keep gaining share, exports recover; EBITDA margin back to ~15% by FY28. Ather valued at a 10% holding discount.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: The weak 2026 monsoon and the end of the GST boost stall entry and deluxe motorcycles, TVS/Bajaj/Ather out-launch VIDA, commodity costs stay high; margins stuck near 13%. Ather valued at a 30% holding discount and Hero FinCorp at 0.7x book.

methods.name: P/E (15x core) + stakes
methods.why: How the street values Hero: P/E on FY28E/Jun-28E core EPS (16-18x: PL 16x, Motilal Oswal, Emkay and Choice 18x) plus the Ather and Hero FinCorp stakes at a 20-30% holding discount. Ours: 15.0x Sep-28E EPS before associates (own forward median since 2021 on that basis 16.4x x 0.931 sector de-rating) plus stakes of ~Rs870 a share (Ather at the 30-Sep close of Rs1,425 less 20%, Hero FinCorp at 1.0x Mar-26 book less 20%, Euler and other holdings at book). ENGINE WORKAROUND: the engine has no add-on line, so the multiple shown is a composite = 15.0x + stakes per share / Sep-28E EPS of each scenario (set by tools/authoring/HEROMOTOCO.stakes.js). Bull core 18x, bear 12.5x.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: 9.0x Sep-28E EBITDA plus model net cash (which carries the stakes at book, not market). Derivation: Hero's 12.9x median trailing EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021 x 0.931 sector de-rating = 12.0x trailing, restated for Sep-28E EBITDA being ~30% above the twelve months to Jun-26 (Rs7,090 cr) = 9.2x, rounded. Bull 10x / bear 8.5x from the 75th/25th percentiles (14.3x, 11.9x) on the same basis.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests cash-flow support: 15-year FCFF, cost of equity 11.6%, terminal growth 5.5%. Net cash includes the stakes at book value.
